questions.question: A man took a loan from a bank at the rate of 20% p.a. simple interest. After 4 years he had to pay Rs. 1600 interest only for the period. Find the principal amount borrowed by him.
questions.explanation:
Let the principal amount be Rs x.

Simple Interest \(= \ \frac{(Principal\  \times \text{\ Rate\ } \times \ Time)}{100}\)

Simple Interest \(\  = \frac{\ (x \times 20 \times 4)}{100}\)

\(= > 1600 = \frac{80x}{100}\)

\(= > 1600 = 0.8x\)

\(= > x = \ Rs\ 2000\)

questions.question: If the principal is Rs.10000 and the rate of interest is 5% per annum for 2 years at simple interest, then find the simple interest on this principal.
questions.explanation:
Simple Interest \(= \ \frac{(Principal\  \times \text{\ Rate\ } \times \ Time)}{100}\)

where:

Principal \(= \ Rs.\ 10,000\)

Rate \(= \ 5\%\ per\ annum\)

Time \(= \ 2\ years\)

Simple Interest\(\  = \ \frac{(10,000\  \times 5\  \times 2)\ }{100}\  = \ Rs.\ 1,000\)

questions.question: If the principal is Rs.10000 and the time for which this principal invested is 3 years. If he gets simple interest of Rs.1800 after 3 years, then find the rate of interest.
questions.explanation:
Simple Interest =( Principal × Rate × Time )100
where:
Principal =Rs·10,000
Rate =R% per annum
Time =3 years
Simple Interest =(10,000×R×3)100
⇒1800=300R
⇒R=6%

questions.question: Mohan invested Rs.30000 and the rate of interest is 12% per annum. If the sum is invested for 4/3 years, then find the total amount he will get after 4/3 years.
questions.explanation:
Simple Interest \(= \ \frac{(Principal\  \times \text{\ Rate\ } \times \ Time)}{100}\)

where:

Principal \(= \ Rs.\ 30,000\)

Rate\(\  = \ 12\%\ per\ annum\)

Time \(= \frac{4}{3}\text{\ years}\)

Simple Interest \(= \ \frac{(30,000 \times \ 12\  \times \ \frac{4}{3})\ }{100}\  = 4800\)

Amount = Principal + SImple Interest

\(= 4800 + 30000 = 34800\)

questions.question: If the principal is Rs.20000 and the time for which this principal is invested is 4 years. If he gets a simple interest of Rs.8000 after 4 years, then find the rate of interest.
questions.explanation:
Simple Interest \(= \ \frac{(Principal\  \times \text{ Rate } \times \ Time)}{100}\)

where:

Principal \(= \ Rs.\ 12,000\)

Rate\(\  = \ R\%\ \ \)

Time = 4 years

Simple Interest \(= \ \frac{(20,000\  \times \text{\ R\ } \times \ 4)}{100}\ \)

\(= > 8000 = 800R\)

\(= > R = \ 10\%\ \)

questions.question: A banker took a loan for Rs.15000 at 10% per annum of simple interest for 5 years and he gave this amount on loan to another person for 5 years who was paying 12% interest to him. Find the overall profit of the banker.
questions.explanation:
Amount banker needs to pay to the bank = \(15000 + \frac{(15000 \times 5 \times 10)}{100}\)

\(= 15000 + 7500\)

\(= 22500\)

Amount he will receive from the person =

\(15000 + \ \frac{(15000 \times 5 \times 12)}{100}\ \)

\(= 15000 + 9000\)

\(= 24000\)

Therefore;

Overall profit\(\ \  = \ 24000 - 22500 = 1500\)

questions.question: If the principal is Rs.40000 and rate of interest is 3% per annum for 4 years and after 4 years find the total amount he will get after 4 years.
questions.explanation:
Simple Interest \(= \ \frac{(Principal\  \times \text{\ Rate\ } \times \ Time)}{100}\)

where:

Principal \(= \ Rs.\ 40000\)

Rate \(= \ 3\%\ per\ annum\)

Time\(\  = \ 4\ years\)

Simple Interest\(\  = \ \frac{(40000\  \times \ 3 \times 4)\ }{100} = 4800\)

Amount = Principal + Simple Interest\(= 40000 + 4800 = \ Rs\ 44800\)

questions.question: If the principal is Rs.20000 and the rate of interest is 10% per annum for 8 years at simple interest, then find the simple interest on this principal.
questions.explanation:
Simple Interest \(= \ \frac{(Principal\  \times \text{\ Rate\ } \times \ Time)}{100}\)

where:

Principal\(\  = \ Rs.\ 20,000\)

Rate \(= \ 10\%\ per\ annum\)

Time\(\  = \ 8\ years\)

Simple Interest\(\  = \ \frac{(10,000\  \times \ 8 \times \ 10)\ }{100}\  = \ Rs.\ 16,000\)

questions.question: Manish invested Rs.25000 in a scheme and in this scheme, he gets Rs.5000 as simple interest which is calculated as 10% per annum for a certain period of time. Find the period of time for which the sum was invested.
questions.explanation:
Simple Interest \(= \ \frac{(Principal\  \times \text{\ Rate\ } \times \ Time)}{100}\)

where:

Principa\(l\  = \ Rs.\ 25,000\)

Rate \(= \ 10\%\ per\ annum\)

Time\(\  = \ T\ years\)

Simple Interest \(= \ (25,000\  \times \text{\ T\ } \times \ 10)\ /\ 100\ \)

\(= > 5000 = 2500T\)

\(= > T = \ 2\ years\)

questions.question: If the principal is Rs.10000 and the rate of interest on this principal is (x+3) % per annum and the time period is x years and the simple interest on this principal is Rs.4000, then find the value of x.
questions.explanation:
Simple Interest \(= \ \frac{(Principal\  \times \text{\ Rate\ } \times \ Time)}{100}\)

where:

Principal \(= \ Rs.\ 10000\)

Rate \(= \ (x + 3)\%\ per\ annum\)

Time\(\  = \ x\ years\)

Simple Interest\(\  = \ \frac{10000\ (x)(x + 3\rbrack\ }{100}\)

\(= > 4000 = 100x(x + 3)\)

\(= > 40 = \ x(x + 3)\ \)

\(= > x^{2} + 3x - 40 = 0\)

\(= > x^{2} + 8x - 5x - 40 = 0\)

\(= > (x + 8)(x - 5) = 0\)

\(= > x = 5\) (as value of cannot be negative)

questions.question: The compound interest on a certain sum for 3 years at 10% per annum is Rs. 6620. Find the simple interest on the same sum for double the time at half the rate percent per annum.
questions.explanation:
Compound Interest \(= \ P\ \{(1\  + \frac{r}{100})^{t} - 1\}\)

\(= > 6620 = P\lbrack(1 + \frac{10}{100})^{3} - 1\rbrack\)

\(= > P\lbrack\frac{(1331 - 1000)}{1000}\rbrack = 6620\)

\(= > \frac{331P}{1000} = 6620\)

\(= > P\  = \ Rs\ 20000\)

Now,

\(T\  = \ 2(3) = \ 6\ years\)

\(R\  = \ \frac{10}{2}\  = \ 5\%\)

So,

SI=P×R×T / 100

=20000×5×6100=6000

questions.question: The difference between the simple interest on a certain sum at the rate of 20% per annum for 2 years and compound interest which is at the same rate is Rs.400. what is the principal?
questions.explanation:
Let the principal be Rs x.

According to question;

SI -Ci\(\  = \ 400\)

\(= > x \times 20 \times \frac{2}{100} - x\lbrack(1 + \frac{20}{100})^{2} - 1\rbrack = 400\)

\(= > \frac{40x}{100}\  - \ \frac{9x}{25} = \ 400\)

\(= > \frac{(40x - 36x)}{100}\  = \ 400\)

\(= > x\  = \ Rs\ 10000\)

questions.question: A scheme offers Rs.24200 amount from the principal of certain amount after 2 years and the rate of the interest given is 10%. Find the compound interest offered by the scheme after 2 years on Principal.
questions.explanation:
\(Amount = \ P\lbrack(1\  + \ \frac{r}{100})^{t}\rbrack\)

So;

P = Rs P, r =10 % per annum, t = 2 years.

Amount\(= \ P\lbrack(1 + \frac{10}{100})^{2}\rbrack\)

\(= > 24200 = P\lbrack(\frac{11}{10})^{2}\rbrack\)

\(= > 24200 = \frac{121P}{100}\)

\(= > P = Rs\ 20000\)

Therefore;

Compound Interest = Amount - Principal

\(= \ 24200 - 20000\)

\(= Rs\ 4200\)

questions.question: If the rate of interest is 8% per annum and the total compound interest after 2 years is Rs.3328, then find the principal.
questions.explanation:
\(Compound\ Interest = \ P\lbrack(1\  + \ \frac{r}{100})^{t} - 1\rbrack\)

So;

P = Rs P, r = 8 % per annum, t = 2 years.

Compound interest \(= \ P\lbrack(1 + \frac{8}{100})^{2} - 1\rbrack\)

\(= > 3328 = P\lbrack(\frac{27}{25})^{2} - 1\rbrack\)

\(= > 3328\  = \ \frac{104P}{625}\)

\(= > P\  = \ Rs\ 20000\)

questions.question: A person has Rs.18000 he invested it for 2 years and after 2 years he gets compound interest on the principal is Rs.7920. Find the rate of interest for which he invested.
questions.explanation:
\(Compound\ Interest = \ P\lbrack(1\  + \ \frac{r}{100})^{t} - 1\rbrack\)

So;

P = Rs. 18,000, r = R % per annum, t = 2 years.

Compound interest \(= \ 30000\lbrack(1 + \frac{R}{100})^{2} - 1\rbrack\)

\(= > 7920 = 30000\lbrack(1 + \frac{R}{100})^{2} - 1\rbrack\)

\(= > \frac{7920}{30000} = (1 + \frac{R}{1000})^{2} - 1\)

\(= > (\frac{44}{100}) + 1 = (1 + \frac{R}{100})^{2}\)

\(= > (\frac{12}{10})^{2} = (1 + \frac{R}{100})^{2}\)

\(= > \frac{12}{10} = 1 + \frac{R}{100}\)

\(= > \frac{1}{5} = \frac{R}{100}\)

\(= > R\  = \ 20\%\)

questions.question: If the principal is Rs.20000 and the rate of interest is 10% per annum for 3 years at compound interest, then find the compound interest on this principal.
questions.explanation:
A\(\  = \ P(1\  + \ \frac{r}{100})^{t}\)

So;

P \(= \ Rs.\ 20,000,\ r\  = \ 10\%\ \)per annum, t \(= \ 3\ years.\)

A \(= \ 20,000(1\  + \ \frac{10}{100})^{3}\)

A\(\  = \ 20,000(1.1)^{3}\)

A\(\  = \ 26620\)

Compound interest = A - P

Compound interest \(= \ 26620 - 20000\)

Compound interest\(\  = \ 6620\)

questions.question: If Rs.10000 becomes Rs.16000 in 6 years at simple interest. What will be the compound interest on Rs. 40,000 after 2 years at the same rate.
questions.explanation:
\(Simple\ Interest\  = \ \frac{(P  \times \text{ R } \times \ T)}{\ 100}\ \)

\(= > 6000 = \frac{\ (10000\  \times \text{ R } \times \ 6)}{100}\ \)

\(R = \ 10\%\)

Now,

\(A = \ P(1\  + \ \frac{R}{100})^{n}\)

\(A = \ 40000(1\  + \ \frac{10}{100})^{2}\)

\(A = \ 48400\)

\(Compound\ Interest\  = \ A\  - \ P\)

\(= \ 48400\  - \ 40000\  = \ 8400\)

questions.question: Find the compound interest on Rs. 25000 in 1 years at 20% per annum, the interest being compounded half-yearly.
questions.explanation:
For half yearly,

Compound Interest \(= P\{(1 + \frac{r}{2 \times 100})^{2t} - 1\}\)

In this case,

P =Rs 25000, r = 20% and t = 1 years

So,

\(CI\  = \ 15000\{\frac{(1 + 20)}{(2 \times 100)^{2}} - 1\}\)

\(= 15000\{(\frac{11}{10})^{2} - 1\}\)

\(= 15000 \times \frac{21}{100}\)

\(= \ Rs\ 3150\)

questions.question: If the principal is Rs.18000 and the rate of interest is 5% per annum for 2 years at compound interest, then find the compound interest on this principal.
questions.explanation:
\(Compound\ Interest = \ P\lbrack(1\  + \ \frac{r}{100})^{t} - 1\rbrack\)

So;

P = Rs 18000, r =5 % per annum, t = 2 years.

Compound interest \(= \ 18000\lbrack(1 + \frac{5}{100})^{2} - 1\rbrack\)

\(= 18000\lbrack(\frac{21}{20})^{2} - 1\rbrack\)

\(= 25000 \times \frac{41}{625}\)

\(= Rs\ 1845\)

questions.question: If the difference between the CI and SI on a certain sum of money is Rs. 135 at 15% per annum for 2 years. Find the Principal value.
questions.explanation:
The difference between CI and SI for 2 years \(= P(\frac{r}{100})^{2}\)

Rate(r)= 15%

ATQ, \(P(\frac{15}{100})^{2} = 135\)

\(P = 135 \times \frac{10000}{225}\)

\(P = 6000.\)

Hence, the Principal Value is Rs 6000.
